from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 4  # sources
    J = 15  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [141, 223, 221, 238]
    demands = [31, 29, 33, 21, 10, 52, 47, 11, 38, 42, 24, 19, 40, 18, 37]
    cost_matrix = [[29.55, 15.73, 3.73, 23.23, 11.69, 15.34, 9.09, 9.22, 12.8, 4.21, 26.42, 20.08, 23.43, 12.84, 9.69], [29.57, 21.06, 5.28, 19.4, 4.8, 18.93, 9.05, 14.35, 28.56, 12.92, 27.21, 29.17, 19.86, 9.89, 22.98], [28.76, 12.34, 23.22, 13.61, 21.94, 25.96, 20.86, 12.77, 8.9, 10.48, 13.24, 24.36, 10.51, 18.5, 5.6], [27.18, 7.64, 22.67, 11.99, 26.25, 20.17, 29.46, 15.83, 18.64, 5.96, 19.91, 13.22, 21.91, 23.3, 29.69]]
    emission_matrix = [[8.56, 11.96, 20.0, 1.99, 15.29, 17.02, 6.97, 10.38, 18.47, 11.86, 4.48, 9.67, 8.38, 9.16, 14.84], [4.08, 8.74, 11.92, 13.63, 15.13, 9.85, 8.71, 5.18, 10.81, 8.36, 4.16, 10.64, 3.46, 13.49, 5.86], [13.1, 12.23, 10.57, 12.62, 9.56, 16.72, 4.86, 15.92, 11.73, 3.96, 5.19, 3.78, 8.8, 5.87, 13.78], [10.94, 5.99, 12.63, 8.96, 12.18, 13.6, 15.63, 3.09, 16.82, 15.73, 3.63, 10.82, 14.43, 16.65, 1.0]]
    fixed_costs = [[182, 257, 148, 94, 268, 228, 74, 79, 222, 291, 187, 51, 103, 230, 172], [124, 226, 134, 297, 59, 214, 89, 65, 148, 257, 293, 184, 145, 147, 94], [93, 231, 172, 243, 86, 94, 166, 81, 269, 105, 255, 271, 187, 70, 145], [114, 87, 143, 221, 203, 65, 268, 240, 199, 262, 140, 186, 281, 230, 188]]
    moq = [[19, 10, 20, 7, 12, 9, 6, 15, 15, 17, 5, 8, 10, 10, 10], [11, 12, 15, 8, 11, 8, 15, 18, 9, 8, 20, 6, 16, 14, 6], [15, 9, 11, 7, 11, 14, 18, 12, 11, 13, 5, 11, 13, 19, 12], [6, 12, 9, 6, 6, 8, 10, 16, 14, 9, 16, 10, 13, 11, 20]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Supply Chain and Sustainability Leadership
From: Director, Sustainability & Logistics
Date: Today
Subject: Balancing shipping cost and carbon to meet store demand under operational rules

Context
We are expanding our use of data-driven routing to deliver reliably while advancing our climate commitments and managing spend. Every warehouse-to-store lane carries both a monetary shipping cost per unit and a carbon impact per unit. In practice, the least expensive lanes are often the most carbon intensive, so treating cost and emissions explicitly—and together—is essential. Our aim is to select a network plan that reflects management’s priorities on cost and sustainability without compromising service.

Operational rules that must be respected
- Route activation fees: Each lane we open incurs a fixed setup expense covering carrier contracting, regulatory paperwork, and dock readiness. This fee is charged when a lane is activated and does not depend on volume shipped.
- Minimum order quantities: Once a lane is activated, we must move at least the required minimum volume on that lane to justify full-truck loading and avoid inefficient handling. If we cannot meet that minimum, the lane should remain inactive.
- Supplier limits per store: To keep receiving manageable and vendor oversight practical, each store may be supplied by no more than the allowed number of distinct warehouses. This cap must be honored in any routing plan.

Management priority
Leadership has defined the relative importance of cost versus emissions. We will apply these weights to the variable (per-unit) components only: the cost weight will be applied to total variable shipping spend, and the emissions weight will be applied to total carbon. Route setup fees will be added in full and will not be scaled by these weights.

Business goal and decision approach
We will identify which lanes to activate and how much to ship on each lane so that:
- Warehouse inventory is not exceeded, and each store’s demand is fully met.
- Any activated lane carries at least its required minimum volume.
- Each store receives from no more than the allowed number of warehouses.

Among all plans that meet these rules, we will select the one with the lowest blended total composed of: the cost weight applied to total variable shipping spend, the emissions weight applied to total carbon, plus the full value of all activated-lane setup fees. This approach makes the trade-off transparent: if a low-cost lane is highly carbon intensive, it will face a higher blended total when emissions are valued more; if a low-emission lane is more expensive, it will be preferred only when the improvement in carbon justifies the added spend. Setup fees and minimum volumes will discourage low-volume lanes that would otherwise look attractive on a per-unit basis. The store supplier cap will streamline receiving and accountability while limiting the number of warehouses that can serve each store.

Next steps
- Validate data on warehouse supply, store demand, lane-level per-unit costs and emissions, lane setup fees, and lane minimums.
- Run network scenarios using management’s weights to surface the preferred activation set and shipment pattern.
- Review trade-offs with Finance and Store Operations, then align on the recommended plan and implementation timeline with Routing, Carriers, and DC leaders.
